precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:19
precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. Spot the signs of lust: a brother telling you at 11 p.m. that he is naked is setting the mood and lining you up. Get the hell off the phone and put him in his place. And ask leadership how he handles correction: “he that hateth reproof is brutish”, and a man who cannot take correction from the men over him has a problem with God.

If you see these signs early, congratulations, sister, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, or wise up and follow counsel? Do nothing without advice, and once you have done it with advice, you will not have to repent of it. Break the cycle.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1-5
precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

thread.label: James 1:25
thread.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10
precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

classes.title: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:1
precepts.why:
“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is basically all you are giving. Some people don’t even understand what faith really is, because faith alone is just saying I believe in something. Paul defines it: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

So don’t tell me you have faith. Faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, what you can see, something materialized. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull; I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see the fruit of it.

Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell where they are going by how they carry themselves. On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-squares and architect tubes. He doesn’t have the degree yet, he is not an architect or engineer yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going. That is how faith is validated by action. Where there is no vision, the people perish; your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head.

That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, meaning it did not exist yet, but he still called it earth, because earth existed in God’s mind. Then the Spirit moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and caused them to form the earth and the light. And he saw that the light was good: he compared what was formed to what he imagined and it agreed with the thought in his mind. Sisters do the same at the mirror; you don’t walk away until what you did with your hands matches the image in your mind, and then you say it is good. That is the power we have, but our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, and we fell asleep for centuries.

That is why the elders must set up organizational foundations, literal buildings where people can see the works of the teaching. A brother or sister naked and destitute of daily food told “Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”, but given nothing, is still hungry. That is church, that is Christianity. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:27
precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

precepts.label: Job 1:10-12
precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.label: John 13:2
precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:22-23
precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 6:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:7
precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12-13
precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. It is when you hate God and retract yourself from the love of the heavenly Father, when you prefer this world, this system and this setup over the guidelines of God, and would rather have this phobia of freedom and be guided by your oppressors.

The scriptures say pride goeth before destruction. When you go contrary to the Lord, death is at your door: “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.”

Your heart is then removed from the one that created you. “And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof”: Esau's rulership is already ordained to pass away. Will you escape when the destruction comes, or pass away with it?

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
John says “the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Who is he that doeth the will of God? David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.

That one abides for ever: you will have everlasting life, and you are going to rule over these kingdoms. Everything you could not see yourself living without in this world shall come to an end, but the one with God's law in his heart abides.

“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”. That is the business we are in: we have to overcome. With rank or without rank, a brother has to stay the same trooper. Don’t bail out now; it is time to stand up and face what we have to face.

What we have to overcome, Paul lays out: “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” Your mother, your father, your aunt, if they are living an unrighteous life, will not inherit the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: not by Christianity, not by religion, not by the white man, not by the uncle or auntie telling you that you are in a cult. Satan can deceive you into leaving this life while you think you are still in the faith.

“Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”. A lot of us are fighting the fornication spirit, the covetous spirit, the lustful demons. “Nor thieves”: some cannot stop stealing even in this truth, like the brother who borrowed the book and never brought it back. “Nor drunkards”: know your limit, because the drink spirit brings out whatever defilement is in your mind.

“And such were some of you.” That is the life we came from, so don’t think Satan won’t tempt you with these things now. And Galatians 6 warns: “if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work”. It is by the grace of God that you stand. That is how we overcome.

He is one “who enlargeth his desire as hell”: he wants the oil, the minerals, the rare earths, the resources. He “is as death”, because when he comes through he brings death. So Death and Hell riding over the fourth part of the earth is America, never satisfied, killing “with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.” War, famine, death, and the beasts of the earth, which is zoonosis: gain-of-function research taking diseases from monkeys, bats and animals and making viruses that kill us. But the question is, do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would be entertaining sin, no way we would allow evil right up under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You mess around and you get slain.

The Lord has his timetable, and we are not on that level. You only see your own point of view; you do not have the Lord’s vantage point, looking at everything on this planet coming into the synchronicity he is waiting for. The angels are holding back whole armies until the sealing is finished, perhaps until that one last brother wakes up. You cannot push him. precepts.why:

But you are not on the Lord’s level. Believe me, the Lord will not be a millisecond late when it comes to sending his angels in to destroy our enemies, and you do not know that time. So in our wanting it, what should we be doing? Making sure we are in the right spiritual and mental space, so that when he sends the angels we are not caught off guard as by a thief in the night. We want to declare his wonderful works with a hundred percent confidence, not nervous that we are still in sin somewhere that has not been found out yet.

The people who say, I don’t need to congregate, I can fellowship at home, say it because they don’t want anybody to see their nasty, wicked evil. When you come in here it is going to show, and righteous brothers and sisters are going to point it out.

Accept that correction, because it is love: the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. Somebody telling you where it is at will keep you out of trouble and set you right for when the Lord does send the angels. The angels are holding the four winds until the servants of God are sealed; make sure you are one of them when the time is made short.

precepts.why:
Visualize the scene of Revelation 7: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds. That wind is not the regular wind that blows every day; it is destruction. The four corners are where the militaries are, straining to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back. Bishop Nathanyel, who is an artist, once drew this scene.

2 Esdras 13 is the same scene. “There arose a wind from the sea, that it moved all the waves thereof. And I beheld, and, lo, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.” That is how Christ is coming back. “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you think he will not see your wicked thoughts and the things you thought you were hiding? “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. So the Lord tells the four angels, hold the four winds; don’t let them fight yet. When Christ comes back these armies will try to fight him to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every last one of them. And if we are not right, he is going to destroy us too. Brothers and sisters, make sure your diligence is on par.

Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. precepts.label: Hebrews 11:25
precepts.why:
Sirach says “Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman”, and it begins with the eyes. Your eyes are directly correlated with your mind; they work in sync, and what you see makes your mind react a certain way. When you see something inappropriate online, not even porn, which is obvious, but something you know is not right, and you find yourself clicking and looking, you are not in control. You are down that rabbit hole looking for that feel good, because sin feels good. It is enjoyable.

That is why Moses is set before us in Hebrews: “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. The pleasure of sin is only for a season, and you are going to pay the price for it. There is a price that is going to be paid.

That little season we deem as pleasure is only pleasure because your mind has convinced you it is, and that is because you have made an agreement with your eyes to keep looking. That is what got David caught up. He did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came along with it.

So the best thing to do is turn away. Turning your head is proof you have control of your members; that is called self-control. If you cannot turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is driving. “For many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, deceived because they looked and did not turn away, when a simple motion of the head could have saved them a world of problems. Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasure; that is the choice set before us.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:27-31
precepts.why:
“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.
